methodology.scope: Every work in works.json and every Arabic file in the local manifest is discoverable in the interactive map. Later-language branches are a smaller, source-backed selection rather than a claim to completeness.
methodology.direct_relation: A documented translation, summary, commentary, edition, or digital collation connected to a specific work or witness.
methodology.influence_relation: A broader Galenic synthesis or teaching collection. It must not be read as descent from one specific Pergamap file.

upstream.title: Hippocrates, Aphorisms
upstream.description: Galen quotes each Hippocratic aphorism and then comments on it. The famous opening, 'Life is short, the art long,' therefore travels inside both the Greek and Arabic commentary traditions.

receptions.title: Ars parva / Tegni
receptions.description: Gerard of Cremona translated Galen's Art of Medicine from Ḥunayn's Arabic, interleaved with Ibn Riḍwān's commentary. It entered the Articella teaching collection in the thirteenth century.

receptions.title: Melakhah qetanah (Small Art)
receptions.description: Samuel ibn Tibbon translated the Art of Medicine and Ibn Riḍwān's commentary from Arabic into Hebrew in 1199. Other Hebrew versions used Latin, including Gerard's Arabic-derived version.

receptions.title: Commenta super Aforismos Ypocratis
receptions.description: Constantine the African's Latin translation of Galen's Commentary on the Aphorisms depends on Ḥunayn's ninth-century Arabic version and circulated in the Articella tradition.

receptions.title: De tactu pulsus
receptions.description: Mark of Toledo translated On the Pulse for Beginners from Arabic into Latin; manuscript colophons explicitly name the Greek-to-Arabic and Arabic-to-Latin stages.

receptions.title: De complexionibus
receptions.description: Gerard of Cremona produced a complete Latin translation of On Temperaments from Arabic. Pergamap currently holds Arabic summaries of this work, not the full Arabic version behind Gerard.

receptions.title: Hebrew Alexandrian Summary of On Sects
receptions.description: Shimshon ben Shlomo translated the Alexandrian summary from Arabic into Hebrew in 1322. The very literal version survives in Vienna, Austrian National Library cod. hebr. 29.

receptions.title: Galen on Medical Experience
receptions.description: Richard Walzer edited the Arabic version and translated it into English. The complete work survives only in Arabic, reached through Ḥubaysh's Arabic translation of Ḥunayn's Syriac version.

receptions.title: Commentary on Hippocrates' Epidemics II
receptions.description: Uwe Vagelpohl and Simon Swain's critical edition translates Ḥunayn's Arabic into English. The Greek original is lost, making Arabic the only intact witness.

receptions.title: Über die medizinischen Namen
receptions.description: Max Meyerhof and Joseph Schacht published Ḥubaysh's Arabic text with a German translation. The Greek original is lost and no complete English translation is currently recorded by Pergamap.

receptions.title: GoHA bilingual critical edition
receptions.description: The GoHA project is building a critical Greek-Arabic edition of the first four books with modern translations and digital access. It is a current scholarly destination for this branch.

context.title: The Articella
context.description: A changing Latin teaching collection that placed Galen's short introductory works and commentaries beside Hippocratic and Arabic medical texts. Some components came through Arabic; others came directly from Greek or older Latin traditions.

context.title: al-Rāzī, Comprehensive Book on Medicine
context.description: Al-Rāzī's reading notes and case observations cite Greek authorities—especially Galen—alongside Islamic writers. It preserves reception and quotation, not a single lineal copy of one Galenic work.

context.title: Ibn Sīnā (Avicenna), Canon of Medicine
context.description: The Canon systematized, criticized, and extended Greek Galenic medicine. Gerard of Cremona's Latin translation became a European university text, but the Canon is an original synthesis rather than a translation of one Pergamap witness.

context.title: The Pantegni
context.description: Constantine the African adapted and translated ʿAlī ibn al-ʿAbbās al-Majūsī's Arabic Complete Book of the Medical Art into Latin. It carried an Islamicate synthesis of classical medicine into Europe, rather than one Galenic text unchanged.
